## Author

**Matthew Crump** is a computational cognitive psychologist at Brooklyn College of CUNY. His lab website is
[crumplab.com](https://crumplab.com), and his ORCID iD is
[0000-0002-5612-0090](https://orcid.org/0000-0002-5612-0090).

MINERVA Space Echo is experimental software: an attempt to hear what a model of human memory does when its
memories are sounds. It was written with help from [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) (Anthropic).

## How to cite

If you use MINERVA Space Echo in research, teaching or music, please cite it:

> Crump, M. J. C. (2026). *MINERVA Space Echo* (Version 0.4.0) [Computer software].
> <https://github.com/CrumpLab/MinervaSpaceEcho>

```bibtex
@software{crump_minerva_space_echo_2026,
  author  = {Crump, Matthew J. C.},
  title   = {{MINERVA Space Echo}},
  year    = {2026},
  version = {0.4.0},
  url     = {https://github.com/CrumpLab/MinervaSpaceEcho}
}
```

The repository's [`CITATION.cff`](https://github.com/CrumpLab/MinervaSpaceEcho/blob/HEAD/CITATION.cff) has the same
details; GitHub turns it into a **Cite this repository** button on the repository page.

The model itself is Douglas Hintzman's MINERVA II; see the references on
[How MINERVA works](concepts/minerva.qmd#further-reading).
